examples.en: That athlete set a monumental achievement by winning three straight Olympic titles.

examples.ko: 이 연구는 한국 의학사의 금자탑으로 평가받아요.
examples.en: This research is regarded as a landmark in Korean medical history.

examples.ko: 오랜 노력 끝에 이룬 금자탑이라 더 값져요.
examples.en: It is a monumental achievement after long effort, so it is even more precious.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 쌓아 올린 금자탑을 절대 잊지 마세요.
examples.en: Never forget the monumental achievement our team built up.

examples.ko: 그 소설은 한국 문학의 금자탑이라고 불려요.
examples.en: That novel is called a monument of Korean literature.

examples.ko: 십 년 만에 금자탑을 이룬 감독의 인터뷰를 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched an interview with the director who achieved a landmark after ten years.

explain: '금자탑을 세우다/쌓다'처럼 큰 업적을 말할 때 주로 써요. 뉴스, 기념사, 소개글에서 자주 보이고, 친구끼리 편하게 말할 때는 '대단한 업적' 정도로 말해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '금자탑을 세우다/쌓다' for a great achievement. You often see it in news, speeches and introductions, while friends in casual talk would just say '대단한 업적'.

examples.ko: 금장 시계를 선물로 받았는데 너무 반짝여요.
examples.en: I got a gold-trimmed watch as a gift and it's so shiny.
There is gold trim around the edge of the plaque.

examples.ko: 이 펜은 뚜껑만 금장으로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: Only the cap of this pen is gold-plated.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 금장 때문에 훨씬 고급스러워 보여요.
examples.en: This bag looks much more luxurious because of the gold trim.
The gold plating wore off, so I took it to a shop for repair.

examples.ko: 책 표지에 금장 글씨를 넣고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to put gold lettering on the book cover.

explain: 시계, 펜, 액세서리처럼 겉에 금색 장식을 한 물건을 말할 때 많이 써요. 진짜 금이 아니라 금도금이나 금색인 경우도 많아서, 가격을 볼 때는 '순금'인지 확인하세요.
explain_en: It is often used for items like watches, pens and accessories with gold-colored decoration on the surface. It is often gold plating or just gold color rather than real gold, so check whether it is '순금' (pure gold) when buying.

examples.ko: 정부가 밤 열 시 이후 외출 금지령을 내렸어요.
examples.en: The government issued a ban on going out after 10 p.m.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 게임 금지령이 아직 안 풀렸어요.
examples.en: The game ban at my house hasn't been lifted yet.
Dad banned my phone, and I'm upset.

examples.ko: 시험 기간에는 친구 만남 금지령이 떨어져요.
examples.en: During exam season, a ban on meeting friends comes down.

examples.ko: 그 책은 한때 금지령 때문에 읽을 수 없었어요.
examples.en: That book couldn't be read for a while because of a ban.
When the ban was lifted, people poured into the square.

explain: '금지령을 내리다', '금지령이 풀리다/해제되다'처럼 짝지어 써요. 나라의 명령뿐 아니라 집에서 부모님이 정한 규칙을 장난스럽게 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It pairs as '금지령을 내리다' and '금지령이 풀리다/해제되다'. Besides official orders, people also use it playfully for rules set by parents at home.

examples.ko: 금쪽같은 내 아들이 드디어 대학에 붙었어요.
examples.en: My precious son finally got into university.
To parents, their children are truly precious.

examples.ko: 금쪽같은 휴가를 비 때문에 다 날렸어요.
examples.en: I lost my precious vacation to the rain.
Grandmother smiled, holding her precious grandchild.
Don't waste your precious time; study.

examples.ko: 금쪽같이 키운 딸이 다음 달에 시집을 가요.
examples.en: The daughter I raised so preciously is getting married next month.

explain: 주로 '금쪽같은 자식/내 새끼/시간'처럼 앞에서 꾸며 줄 때 써요. 아끼는 마음이 아주 큰 말이라 자식이나 소중한 시간에 많이 쓰고, 물건에는 덜 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly used before a noun, as in '금쪽같은 자식/내 새끼/시간'. It carries a strong feeling of cherishing, so it is common for children and precious time, and less so for objects.

examples.ko: 놀이기구가 급강하하자 탑승객들이 일제히 비명을 질렀어요.
examples.en: When the ride dropped suddenly, the riders all screamed together.
The temperature is plunging, so dress warmly.
I screamed on the ride that drops suddenly.
The bird suddenly dove down when it saw food.
Hold the handle tightly in the steep-drop section.
I'm worried the stock price will drop sharply in the afternoon.

explain: 실제로는 '급강하하다'로 많이 쓰고, 기온, 비행기, 놀이기구, 주가처럼 갑자기 크게 내려가는 것에 써요. 값이나 인기가 내려갈 때는 '급락'을 써요.
explain_en: In practice it is mostly used as the verb '급강하하다', for temperature, planes, rides and stock prices that suddenly fall a lot. For prices or popularity falling, use '급락'.

examples.en: My father was ill, so I rushed down to my hometown.
The boss canceled the business trip and came back in a hurry.
Hearing the news, I rushed to the hospital.
They say the national team coach is returning home in haste.

examples.ko: 회의가 급거 열려서 준비를 못 했어요.
examples.en: The meeting was called in haste, so I couldn't prepare.
My friend had to move suddenly in a rush.

explain: '급거 귀국하다', '급거 소집하다'처럼 갑작스러운 일 때문에 서둘러 움직일 때 써요. 뉴스나 글에서 주로 보이고, 말할 때는 '급하게', '서둘러'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when someone moves in a hurry because of a sudden matter, as in '급거 귀국하다'. It appears mainly in news and writing; in speech people say '급하게' or '서둘러'.

examples.en: House prices are showing a sharp upward trend these days.
Gas prices turned sharply upward, so the burden is big.
There was news that the sharp rise has lost some steam.
The sharp rise in vegetable prices is due to the rainy season.
I was startled by the surge and sold my stocks.
It's in a sharp rise now, so I'm afraid to buy.

explain: '급등세를 보이다/타다/이어가다'처럼 값이 빠르게 오르는 흐름을 말할 때 써요. 반대말은 '급락세'이고, 뉴스에서 집값, 주가, 환율 이야기에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It describes a fast upward trend, as in '급등세를 보이다/타다/이어가다'. The opposite is '급락세', and it appears in news about house prices, stocks and exchange rates.

examples.en: Stock prices continue to fall sharply.
The sharp drop won't stop, so I'm anxious.
The exchange rate turned into a steep decline from yesterday.
Even amid the slump, this shop has many customers.
The crypto market's sharp decline has lasted a week.
It's in free-fall now, so I decided not to sell.

explain: 값이나 수치가 빠르게 떨어지는 흐름을 말해요. '급락세를 보이다/이어가다/멈추다'처럼 쓰고, 반대말은 '급등세'예요.
explain_en: It describes a fast downward trend in prices or numbers. It is used as '급락세를 보이다/이어가다/멈추다', and the opposite is '급등세'.

examples.ko: 이 종목은 급상승 뒤에 급락하는 일이 잦아요.
examples.en: This stock often plunges after a sharp rise.

examples.ko: 코인 가격이 급락해서 손해를 본 친구가 많아요.
examples.en: Crypto prices plunged, and many friends lost money.
The stock price suddenly plunged yesterday.
In winter, the temperature often drops sharply.
When popularity plunges, advertising also decreases.

examples.ko: 급락한 가격에 물건을 사려는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people want to buy at the sharply reduced price.

explain: '떨어지다'보다 훨씬 갑작스럽고 크게 내려갈 때 써요. 주가, 가격, 기온, 인기에 쓰고 반대말은 '급등하다'예요.
explain_en: It is much more sudden and large than '떨어지다' (to fall). It is used for stock prices, prices, temperature and popularity, and the opposite is '급등하다'.

examples.ko: 정부의 정책이 급선회를 해서 모두 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The government's policy made a sudden turn, and everyone was surprised.

examples.ko: 운전자가 급선회를 하는 바람에 차가 크게 흔들렸어요.
examples.en: The driver turned sharply, so the car shook a lot.

examples.ko: 회사의 급선회로 해외 진출이 갑자기 결정됐어요.
examples.en: The company's sudden change of course led to a sudden decision to expand overseas.

examples.ko: 비행기의 급선회는 승객에게 위험할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A sharp turn of a plane can be dangerous for passengers.
The team members were very flustered by this sudden turn.
Thanks to the sharp turn, I barely avoided an accident.

explain: 차, 배, 비행기가 갑자기 방향을 바꿀 때도 쓰고, 정책이나 계획의 방향이 갑자기 달라질 때도 써요. 뉴스에서는 '정책 급선회'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when a car, ship or plane suddenly changes direction, and also when a policy or plan suddenly changes course. In the news it often appears like '정책 급선회'.

examples.en: The typhoon suddenly changed direction and went west.
The car in front turned sharply, so I was startled.
The company made a sharp turn toward going overseas.
If public opinion suddenly swings, policy changes too.
Hold the handle when the boat turns sharply.
Citizens were flustered by the government's sharply changed policy.

explain: 움직이는 것이 방향을 확 바꿀 때와 계획이나 방침이 갑자기 달라질 때 모두 써요. 방침이나 여론을 말할 때는 '급선회하다'가 '바뀌다'보다 훨씬 갑작스러운 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used both when a moving thing suddenly changes direction and when a plan or policy suddenly shifts. For policies or opinion, it feels much more abrupt than '바뀌다'.

examples.en: The drought was severe, so a water truck came to the village.

examples.ko: 급수차 앞에 주민들이 물통을 들고 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: Residents lined up with water containers in front of the water truck.
I got water from the water truck and washed the kids.
The fire station agreed to send a water truck.

examples.ko: 급수차는 하루에 두 번 오는 것 같아요.
examples.en: The water truck seems to come twice a day.
Boil the water you get from the water truck before drinking.

explain: 가뭄이나 단수, 공사로 수돗물이 안 나올 때 물을 실어 와 나눠 주는 차예요. 뉴스에서 재난이나 단수 이야기가 나올 때 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It is a truck that brings and distributes water when tap water is unavailable because of drought, outages or construction. You often hear it in news about disasters or water cuts.

examples.en: This month's pay is lower than I expected.
How much is left after subtracting tax from the pay?
The company sends the pay on the 25th of every month.
The insurance premium varies depending on the salary amount.
A new employee's pay differs from company to company.

examples.ko: 급여액과 실제로 받는 돈은 조금 달라요.
examples.en: The stated pay and the money you actually receive are a bit different.

explain: 월급이라는 말보다 서류나 회사에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 친구끼리는 '월급'이라고 하고, 급여 명세서나 계약서에서는 '급여액'을 자주 봐요.
explain_en: It is a more formal word than '월급', used in documents and by companies. Friends say '월급', while '급여액' is common on pay stubs and contracts.

examples.en: The sky suddenly darkened and then it rained.
A message came all of a sudden, so I postponed the plan.
My father suddenly decided to move.

examples.ko: 급작스레 찾아온 손님 때문에 정신이 없었어요.
examples.en: I was flustered because of the guest who showed up out of the blue.
The weather turned cold suddenly, so I caught a cold.

examples.ko: 친구가 급작스레 유학을 가겠다고 해서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised when my friend suddenly said they'd study abroad.

explain: '갑자기'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 더 글 같은 느낌이고, 예상 못 한 일이 닥친 느낌이 조금 더 강해요. 보통 말할 때는 '갑자기'를 훨씬 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '갑자기' but sounds more written and slightly stronger in the sense of something unexpected hitting. In everyday speech, '갑자기' is used much more.

examples.en: The car ahead braked suddenly, so I stopped too.

examples.ko: 급제동 때문에 버스 안 사람들이 휘청했어요.
examples.en: People on the bus staggered because of the sudden braking.

examples.ko: 급제동할 때 안전벨트가 몸을 잡아 줘요.
examples.en: The seat belt holds your body when you brake suddenly.
A child ran out, and I barely avoided it by braking hard.

examples.ko: 급제동은 도로가 젖었을 때 특히 위험해요.
examples.en: Sudden braking is especially dangerous when the road is wet.
The luggage spilled forward from the sudden braking.

explain: '급제동을 걸다/하다'처럼 써요. 자동차, 버스, 기차가 갑자기 멈출 때 쓰는 말이라 교통사고 뉴스나 운전 이야기에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is used as '급제동을 걸다/하다'. It describes cars, buses and trains stopping suddenly, so it often appears in traffic accident news and driving talk.

examples.en: I threw the materials together the night before the presentation.
It's a hastily made plan, so it has many gaps.

examples.ko: 손님이 갑자기 와서 반찬을 급조해 냈어요.
examples.en: Guests came suddenly, so I whipped up some side dishes.

examples.ko: 이런 일은 급조하면 꼭 문제가 생겨요.
examples.en: If you rush this kind of work, problems always come up.
Let's not put a team together in a rush; let's prepare slowly.

examples.ko: 급조할 시간이 없어서 있는 걸로 했어요.
examples.en: There was no time to improvise, so I used what I had.

explain: 서둘러 대충 만들었다는 느낌이 있어서 좋은 뜻으로는 잘 안 써요. '급조한 느낌이 나다'처럼 완성도가 떨어진다고 말할 때 자주 나와요. '임시로 만들다'보다 서두른 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It carries a sense of making something quickly and roughly, so it is rarely positive. It often appears when saying something feels rushed, like '급조한 느낌이 나다'. It stresses the hurry more than '임시로 만들다' (to make temporarily).

examples.ko: 이번 개정은 점진적 변화이지 급진적 개혁이 아니에요.
examples.en: This revision is a gradual change, not a radical reform.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 생각은 너무 급진적이라서 반대가 많아요.
examples.en: His ideas are too radical, so there is a lot of opposition.
Radical change makes people uneasy.

examples.ko: 저는 급진적으로 바꾸기보다 조금씩 고치고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'd rather fix things little by little than change them drastically.

examples.ko: 급진적 주장을 하는 학생이 토론에서 인기가 많았어요.
examples.en: The student who made radical claims was popular in the debate.

examples.ko: 회사는 급진적이지 않은 방법으로 비용을 줄였어요.
examples.en: The company cut costs with a non-radical method.

explain: 변화가 빠르고 과감하거나 생각이 아주 앞서 있을 때 써요. 반대말은 '점진적'이고, '급진적인 개혁', '급진적으로 바꾸다'처럼 '-인', '-으로'를 붙여 많이 써요.
explain_en: It describes change that is fast and bold, or ideas that are far ahead. The opposite is '점진적', and it is often used with '-인' or '-으로', as in '급진적인 개혁' and '급진적으로 바꾸다'.

examples.en: The negotiations between the two countries advanced rapidly.
As the talks progressed rapidly, an agreement drew near.

examples.ko: 병의 치료가 급진전해서 다음 주에 퇴원해요.
examples.en: The treatment progressed quickly, so I'm leaving the hospital next week.
I didn't expect their relationship to move so fast.
Things are moving fast, so we need to prepare quickly.

examples.ko: 연구가 급진전한 덕분에 곧 결과가 나와요.
examples.en: Thanks to the research moving ahead quickly, results will come soon.

explain: 협상, 관계, 수사, 연구처럼 오래 멈춰 있던 일이 갑자기 빠르게 앞으로 나아갈 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '관계가 급진전하다'처럼 자주 나오고, 일상에서는 '확 빨라지다'처럼도 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when something that was stalled, like talks, a relationship or research, suddenly moves ahead quickly. News often says '관계가 급진전하다', and in daily talk people also say '확 빨라지다'.

examples.en: The company rushed a technician to the site.
They say the government rushed a rescue team to the area.
We have to send a reporter urgently to the scene.
The head office decided to send staff urgently.
The team that was rushed there arrived late at night.

examples.ko: 지원 인력을 급파하면 피해를 줄일 수 있어요.
examples.en: If we send support staff right away, we can reduce the damage.

explain: '보내다'보다 훨씬 급하게, 긴급한 일을 해결하러 사람을 보낼 때 써요. 주로 뉴스나 회사 업무에서 쓰고, 보내는 대상은 보통 사람이나 팀이에요.
explain_en: It is much more urgent than '보내다' (to send) and is used when sending people to deal with an emergency. It mainly appears in news and business, and the object is usually a person or team.

examples.ko: 급행열차를 타려면 급행료를 따로 내야 해요.
examples.en: To take the express train, you have to pay an express fee separately.
I asked at the station how much the express fare is.
I paid a rush fee to get the documents faster.

examples.ko: 급행료 덕분에 이틀 일찍 비자를 받았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the rush fee, I got my visa two days early.
Including the express fee, the cost is double.

examples.ko: 급행료 없는 일반 배송으로 보내 주세요.
examples.en: Please send it by regular delivery without a rush fee.

explain: 더 빠른 열차나 빠른 처리를 위해 따로 내는 돈이에요. 기차뿐 아니라 서류, 비자, 배송처럼 빨리 받으려고 내는 추가 요금에도 쓰여요.
explain_en: It is an extra charge paid for a faster train or faster processing. Besides trains, it is used for surcharges on documents, visas and delivery when you want speed.

examples.ko: 신부님은 긍휼을 품고 가난한 이들을 돌보셨어요.
examples.en: The priest cared for the poor with compassion in his heart.
Lord, please have mercy on us.
I could feel compassion in his eyes.

examples.ko: 어려운 사람에게 긍휼을 베푸는 일은 아름다워요.
examples.en: Showing compassion to those in need is beautiful.

examples.ko: 긍휼의 마음이 없으면 남을 도울 수 없어요.
examples.en: Without a heart of compassion, you can't help others.

examples.ko: 판사는 긍휼에 호소하는 말에 마음이 흔들렸어요.
examples.en: The judge was moved by words appealing to compassion.

explain: '긍휼히 여기다', '긍휼을 베풀다'처럼 약한 처지의 사람을 안타깝게 보고 돕는 마음을 말해요. 종교 글과 기도에서 자주 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '불쌍히 여기다', '동정하다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used as '긍휼히 여기다' or '긍휼을 베풀다' for a heart that pities and helps those in a weak position. It appears often in religious writing and prayers, while daily talk more often uses '불쌍히 여기다' or '동정하다'.

examples.en: I learned that steel is a key industry of the nation.

examples.ko: 정부는 기간산업을 지키기 위해 지원금을 줘요.
examples.en: The government gives subsidies to protect key industries.

examples.ko: 전기와 철도 같은 기간산업은 국가가 관리해요.
examples.en: Basic industries like electricity and railways are managed by the state.
If key industries shake, the whole economy gets hard.
My father worked in a basic industry field for 30 years.
Investing in basic industries requires a lot of money.

explain: 전기, 철강, 철도, 에너지처럼 다른 산업과 나라 경제의 바탕이 되는 산업을 말해요. 경제 수업이나 뉴스에서 '기간산업 보호', '기간산업 지원'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to industries like electricity, steel, railways and energy that form the base of other industries and the national economy. It appears in economics classes and news as '기간산업 보호' or '기간산업 지원'.

examples.en: During college, I stayed at my uncle's house.
Grandfather lives alone in a small room.
He lived at a temple while writing the book.
The dormitory where the international students live is next to the school.
I haven't decided yet where to stay.
Would it be okay if I stayed at your place for a while?

explain: '살다'나 '지내다'보다 글 같고 점잖은 말이에요. 어디에 머물며 생활하는지를 말할 때 써서, 임시로 머무는 집이나 절, 기숙사 같은 곳에 잘 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '살다', '지내다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is more formal and written than '살다' or '지내다'. It is used for where someone stays and lives, fitting temporary places like a relative's house, temple or dorm. In daily conversation, people usually say '살다' or '지내다'.

examples.ko: 한 번 이겼다고 기고만장해서 연습도 안 해요.
examples.en: He's so full of himself after one win that he doesn't even practice.
My younger sibling got cocky after being praised.
If you get too cocky, it's easy to make mistakes.
He boasted with a cocky look on his face.
The newcomer acted cocky and got scolded.
Don't get cocky just because your grades went up.

explain: 주로 '기고만장하다' 꼴로 써서, 잘나가거나 칭찬을 받고 우쭐해서 거만하게 구는 모습을 말해요. 좋은 뜻이 아니라 흉보거나 주의를 줄 때 쓰고, 비슷한 말로 '우쭐하다', '으스대다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '기고만장하다', describing someone acting arrogant and cocky after succeeding or being praised. It is negative, used for criticizing or warning, and similar words include '우쭐하다' and '으스대다'.
